questions.q: Which standard object holds the specific equipment products attached to one deal at Cascade?
options: Campaign
Opportunity Product (Line Item)
Lead
Task
questions.explain: The lesson explains Opportunity Product (Line Item) attaches specific products, quantities, and prices to one Opportunity -- this is what makes an equipment package concrete.

questions.q: What does the Installation Project custom object track, and why does the standard object model fall short here?
options: Employee time-off requests, because Salesforce has no HR object
The on-site installation lifecycle after an Opportunity is won -- a site, a date, a status, and an installer -- which no standard object models
Marketing campaign budgets, because Campaign has no cost field
Price book entries, because Product has no pricing field
questions.explain: The lesson states standard objects stop at 'deal closed'; Installation Project was built specifically to track the on-site lifecycle -- site address, target install date, install status, and lead installer -- after a won Opportunity.

questions.q: Why are Installation Project and Service Contract built as Lookup relationships rather than Master-Detail?
options: Lookup relationships are required for any custom object in Salesforce
Master-Detail relationships cannot reference the Account object
An installation or contract needs to exist, be reassigned, and be shared on its own terms, not strictly tied to a parent's ownership and security
Lookup relationships automatically roll up currency fields, which Master-Detail cannot do
questions.explain: The lesson explains that Lookup was chosen because these records need to be able to outlive or stand independent of record-level ownership and sharing tied strictly to a parent -- which matters for the sharing-rule design in Lesson 4.

questions.q: In Cascade's object-relationship diagram, what does a won Opportunity produce?
options: A new Lead record
A Campaign Member record
An Installation Project
A duplicate Account
questions.explain: The diagram shows Opportunity --(won)--> Installation Project: a won deal produces an Installation Project that tracks the on-site work that follows.

questions.q: What is the Annual Value field on Service Contract used for, according to this lesson?
options: Calculating the Lead's qualification score
Setting the Opportunity's close probability
Chapter 4 reporting on recurring maintenance revenue
Determining which profile a Contact is assigned
questions.explain: The field table notes Annual Value is a Currency field 'used in Chapter 4 reporting' -- it captures the yearly value of a recurring service contract.
